entries.claim: The desktop client owns a closed draft-2020-12 schema and recognized fixture for GET /api/desktop/v1/bootstrap with schema version 1, minimum client version 0.1.0 and six false capability declarations.

The desktop handoff requires first-party browser authorization, account and usage reads, account-scoped models and pricing, a billing comparison using fixed USD/CNY 6.75, and a first-party wallet URL; it explicitly forbids fabricated values and direct payment handling in the client.

entries.claim: At baseline commit 33926b6c, the Gin API router has anonymous status and pricing routes but no /api/desktop/v1/bootstrap route.

The current fork already provides revocable rotating user_sessions, bearer dashboard authentication, safe self-user projection, user log queries, account-scoped model queries, pricing data, and a first-party wallet route; pending device authorization state is not present.
The product owner authorized submitting the minimal desktop bootstrap handshake now, while keeping account authorization, balances, usage and tool-key management out of this change.

The product owner authorized directly completing the NewAPI desktop interfaces after reviewing the newly submitted repository, while preserving the prior boundary that production deployment is separate.

decisions.question: What server capability may be implemented for the desktop client in this release unit?
decisions.choice: Implement only the anonymous, read-only GET /api/desktop/v1/bootstrap v1 handshake and its closed contract documentation. Return every future capability as false. Do not add authentication, account, usage, pricing projection, tool-key management, database, migration, payment or deployment behavior.

decisions.question: What server capability may supersede the recognition-only desktop bootstrap release unit?
decisions.choice: Add a versioned desktop v2 API with Redis-backed five-minute first-party device authorization, existing user_sessions for desktop access and refresh tokens, authenticated account/usage/models/pricing/billing-comparison projections, and a first-party wallet URL. Keep desktop tool-key management disabled, add no database schema or migration, do not process payment in the desktop API, and do not deploy from this release unit.

requirements.statement: The server exposes one anonymous, read-only desktop bootstrap v1 response that exactly matches the frozen client schema and declares every not-yet-implemented capability as false.
acceptance: GET /api/desktop/v1/bootstrap returns HTTP 200, application/json and the exact closed v1 response without authentication.
The response contains no account, credential, cookie, device code, refresh token, price, wallet URL or backend configuration.
All six future capability flags remain false and repeated or concurrent reads remain equivalent.
Unsupported methods do not mutate state and a subsequent valid GET still returns the recognized response.
No database schema, migration, payment, deployment or existing API behavior changes in this release unit.

requirements.statement: The server exposes a versioned desktop v2 integration that lets a desktop client obtain a dedicated revocable session through explicit first-party browser approval and then read truthful account, usage, available-model, pricing, billing-comparison and wallet-link projections without adding database schema or handling payment inside the desktop API.
acceptance: The immutable v1 bootstrap remains unchanged while /api/desktop/v2/bootstrap advertises only implemented v2 capabilities and keeps tool_keys_manage false.
A device code is stored only in Redis for five minutes, must be approved by a live browser session, is polling-rate limited and can issue at most one desktop session.
Desktop refresh-token rotation and logout reuse existing user_sessions; refresh secrets are returned only to the desktop exchange/refresh caller and are never placed in a URL or log.
Authenticated read endpoints derive account, usage, models and pricing from the same existing owners used by the web dashboard and expose no prompt or response content.

Billing comparison uses the same consume-log cohort for site and reconstructed official cost, fixed USD/CNY 6.75, excludes non-comparable subscription records, and reports coverage instead of fabricating savings.
The wallet endpoint returns only the first-party /wallet/ URL and the desktop API does not accept payment details or payment callbacks.
No model, migration, database schema, deployment, Nginx or production configuration file changes belong to this release unit.

invariants: Bootstrap recognition grants no account session, credential access, configuration write, pricing truth or tool compatibility authority.
A capability is true only after a separate frozen contract and verified implementation release unit exists.

Desktop v2 device authorization is five-minute Redis-only state; approval requires a live browser session and successful exchange creates an ordinary revocable user_session with login_method desktop_device.
The v2 bootstrap maps account, usage, model, pricing and tool-key capabilities to existing authenticated NewAPI owners rather than creating duplicate desktop tables.

contracts.compatibility: Version 1 is a closed response. New fields, capability names or schema versions require a new versioned contract before server and client changes.

contracts.authorization: Anonymous POST with the existing anonymous body-size and rate-limit middleware; unavailable unless Redis is configured.
contracts.idempotency: Each successful call creates a distinct five-minute authorization; retries create a new code and do not reuse prior codes.
contracts.compatibility: V2 only; values are opaque and clients must honor expires_in and interval.

contracts.authorization: Authenticated live browser user_session only; PAT credentials cannot approve a desktop device.
contracts.idempotency: A repeated identical decision returns the existing status; a conflicting later decision is rejected.
contracts.compatibility: V2 only; decision is a closed approve or deny enum.

observability.correlation: Existing authenticated request correlation applies without logging user_code.
observability.audit: The eventual user_session records desktop_device; denied and expired codes leave no database row.
observability.metrics: Count approved, denied and expired outcomes only.

contracts.authorization: Anonymous POST authenticated by the high-entropy device_code; pending exchange is rate limited and successful exchange is one-time.
contracts.idempotency: Pending polls are safe; one approved code can create at most one user_session. A lost successful response requires a new authorization rather than replaying a refresh secret.
contracts.compatibility: V2 only; clients handle authorization_pending, slow_down, access_denied, expired_token and already_used codes.

outputSchema.description: Dedicated desktop access and refresh credentials.

refresh_token.description: Rotating refresh secret stored only by the desktop credential vault.

observability.correlation: Existing request correlation applies; credential values are excluded from logs.
observability.audit: Successful exchange creates the existing user_sessions row with login_method desktop_device.
observability.metrics: Count pending, slow-down, denied, expired, used and issued outcomes without values.

errorSemantics: Polling too quickly returns slow_down and a retry interval.
Denied, expired and consumed codes never issue credentials.

contracts.authorization: Possession of the rotating desktop refresh token and matching session_id.
contracts.idempotency: Existing user_sessions refresh rotation and bounded replay window apply.
contracts.compatibility: V2 JSON transport reuses existing session semantics without cookies.

observability.correlation: Existing authentication correlation applies without token logging.
observability.audit: Existing user_sessions last-active and rotation state remain authoritative.
observability.metrics: Existing auth outcome metrics apply without token values.

errorSemantics: Invalid, expired, revoked, mismatched or reused refresh tokens return the existing closed authentication error codes.
A failed rotation does not expose a replacement secret.

contracts.authorization: A live desktop bearer access token backed by user_sessions; PAT credentials are rejected.
contracts.idempotency: A session can be revoked once; later access is unauthorized.
contracts.compatibility: V2 route reuses existing session revocation semantics and does not delete API tool keys.

observability.audit: The existing user_sessions row records revoked state and reason desktop_logout.

errorSemantics: PAT or missing session credentials are forbidden.
Revocation never deletes or changes tool keys.

packages.objective: Implement the versioned desktop v2 bootstrap, Redis-only browser-approved device authorization, JSON desktop refresh/logout adapters, and the authenticated browser approval surface while mapping all read and tool-key capabilities to existing NewAPI APIs.
deliverables: Immutable v1 plus a closed v2 bootstrap with exact existing route mappings and fixed comparison rate 6.75.
Five-minute Redis-only device authorization with explicit live-browser approval, bounded polling and single session issuance.
Desktop JSON refresh and current-session revocation backed by existing user_sessions.
Authenticated browser approval page that displays the user code and client name and requires explicit approve or deny.
Contract, route, concurrency, replay, expiry, refresh, revocation and browser behavior tests.
nonGoals: No database schema, migration, duplicate account table, duplicate billing data, payment processing, deployment, Nginx or production configuration change.
No new tool-key table or desktop-specific read projections; v2 advertises the existing authenticated owners.
No client repository change in this server release unit.

migrationPolicy.dataBackfill: No schema or customer-data migration. Pending authorization exists only in Redis for five minutes; successful sessions use the existing user_sessions table.
migrationPolicy.rollback: Remove v2 routes and approval UI. Existing v1 and user_sessions remain valid; pending Redis keys expire naturally.

compatibilityPolicy.strategy: Keep desktop bootstrap v1 byte-for-byte compatible and add an independent v2 contract with minimum desktop version 0.2.0.
compatibilityPolicy.supportedVersions: desktop-bootstrap@v1 remains recognition-only; desktop integration v2 adds device authorization and session adapters while reusing existing authenticated APIs.
compatibilityPolicy.removalGate: V1 removal or v2 semantic change requires a successor version and frozen release unit.

requiredAcceptanceScenarios.assertion: V1 stays exact while v2 advertises only implemented existing routes, fixed 6.75 and live Redis availability.
A browser-approved unexpired device code issues one dedicated desktop user_session and no new table.
Missing Redis, malformed codes, pending, slow-down, denied and expired states never issue credentials.
Concurrent exchange of one approved code creates at most one session and later replay is rejected.
Desktop refresh rotates the secret and logout revokes only the current session while a failed refresh remains recoverable under existing semantics.
The authenticated approval page shows code and client identity, requires explicit action and handles success, denial, expiry and API failure without exposing device_code.

stopConditions: Any implementation requires a database schema or migration.
Any credential would be placed in a URL, browser storage, log or response other than the one-time desktop exchange/refresh body.
A read or tool-key capability cannot be mapped to an existing authenticated API owner.
V1 compatibility changes or the approval flow can create more than one session per device code.
Deployment or production configuration becomes necessary.
